predecessors.name: Melayu Kingdom
predecessors.text: Dharmasraya and the Minangkabau highlands: 'in 1347 Adityawarman proclaimed himself king in Malayapura'

successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: the Minangkabau highlands, where the last sultan was arrested on 2 May 1833 and the Dutch took over

ledger.x: 1347: Adityawarman proclaims himself king in Malayapura.

c. 1609: Aceh's governors take the west coast. 'In the early 17th century, the kingdom was forced to recognise the sovereignty of the Sultanate of Aceh'; the page gives no year, 1609 is the step the sultanate-of-aceh dossier uses (it carries the matching gain and a vassal span of Pagaruyung to 1666).
c. 1665: the Minang of the west coast rise against Aceh. 'around 1665, the Minang people on the west coast rose up and rebelled against the Aceh governors'; the VOC had first arrived in 1663.
1666: Aceh is expelled from the west coast.
1803: the Padri civil war begins in the highlands.
4 March 1822: the Dutch drive the Padri out of Pagaruyung.
1833: the sultan's arrest ends the kingdom's part in the Padri War.
2 May 1833: the Dutch take the highlands.
1833: the Pagaruyung Kingdom ends with the sultan's arrest.

wars.name: Padri War
wars.outcome: The Padri occupied Pagaruyung in 1815; the Minangkabau nobility allied with the Dutch in 1821, the Dutch pushed the Padri out of Pagaruyung on 4 March 1822, the sultan was arrested on 2 May 1833, and 'on 16 August 1837, Fort Bonjol was completely conquered'.

wars.name: Minang rising against Aceh and the VOC expulsion of Aceh
wars.outcome: 'expelling the Sultanate of Aceh from the coast of West Sumatra in 1666'; the VOC letter of 9 October 1668 reports it had taken the coast.

wars.name: Majapahit expedition against Pagaruyung (possible)
wars.outcome: 'Majapahit possibly sent another expedition to conquer the kingdom in 1409'; no result stated.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the highlands are a mountain core with undated rantau.
